analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a genuine consumer electricals franchise with strong brand equity in fans and appliances, but the 2022 Butterfly Gandhimathi acquisition created earnings volatility and temporary balance sheet stress that is still normalising. At 34x trailing P/E with net profit still below its 2021 peak, the price asks for perfection in a business that hasn't yet delivered it.
key_strengths: Balance sheet has been aggressively cleaned up — D/E down from 0.65 (2022) to just 0.05; borrowings reduced from INR 1,686 Cr to INR 186 Cr in three years
Consumer-facing brand with broad product range (fans, pumps, lighting, appliances) offering steady, repeat demand — exactly the kind of predictable business I like
Free cash flow consistently positive (INR 635 Cr in FY25) and operating cash flow positive every year for 5 years
key_risks: No meaningful promoter holding — the company is effectively institutionally held (DII 65.7%, FII 20.6%), which removes the owner-operator accountability I value most
Net profit of INR 564 Cr in FY25 is still below the INR 617 Cr earned in FY21 — four years of earnings stagnation is not steady compounding
Operating margin at 7.99% is thin and at the low edge of my comfort zone; any raw material or competitive pressure can easily compress it further
red_flags: Butterfly acquisition inflated debt to INR 1,686 Cr and caused finance costs to spike to INR 109 Cr in FY23 — raises questions about capital allocation discipline
Revenue CAGR of only 9.8% over 7 years, with net profit CAGR of 8.2% — a consumer brand of this scale should be doing better
No promoter stake data available; institutional-only ownership with no founder/promoter creates governance uncertainty
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crompton is a solid consumer electricals business — the kind of boring, everyday-use product company I respect. The balance sheet cleanup since 2022 has been commendable, and the business generates real cash. However, the Butterfly acquisition was expensive and disrupted earnings for nearly four years, which tells me the capital allocation discipline needs watching. Operating margins barely scrape 8%, and with no promoter holding, there is no single aligned owner to hold management accountable over the long run.

At 34x P/E with earnings still below 2021 levels, the market is pricing in a strong recovery that hasn't fully materialised. I would want to see margins back above 10%, net profit convincingly above INR 700 Cr, and clearer evidence of post-acquisition synergies before paying this price. Existing holders may hold, but this is not the 'obvious compounder at fair value' entry point I look for.
